reviews.review:
I tried playing this game without being affected by the reviews and unfortunately I feel like I've wasted my time.

For starters, the entire game is just 10% main story and the other 90% side quests, relationship quests and tasks. I have about 40 hours in the game, most of which I've spent grinding these quests which are mostly copy pasted with different storylines. For example, fetch quests (go here, grab that and bring it back to me), go there and beat these guys up or go to these 3 different planets all with 20 second long departing cutscenes to grab one thing and then return to me to do all of it again. It really stops being fun after the first 20 tasks. The relationship quests are fine I suppose, it's usually tied to another important quest so you're kind of forced into doing them.

My next issue is with the bugs: there are the small ones like companions spawning in the air, the light not working properly and turning the whole screen white or the companions facial expressions freezing mid convo making them look shell shocked for no reason. There are then the large ones like getting stuck in debris, some conversations happening wayyyy later than they should (for example one npc talks about a planet like its not been colonized yet despite it already being colonized 4 hours ago etc.) and Ryder's bodymovements getting stiff for no reason like he doesn't have bones in his body for whatever reason.

The story all in all is fine however you won't probably get through all of it because of how boring and sluggish the whole game feels. As I said, I spent over 40 hours in this game and already forgot what was happening so if that's not a dealbreaker I don't know what is.

One of the last things I want to note is the romance in this game. The developers have polished about 1 romance out of all of the romances in the game. Most of them aren't even worth getting into because they last for about 2 dialogue lines and one loyalty quest (not even that if they're not a member of the tempest) and the next time you'll ever get to talk to them is at the end of the game. Definitely not worth it.

All in all, this game is a huge downgrade from the original Mass Effect trilogy and I highly don't suggest playing it. It's brought interesting ideas into the narrative but those ideas have been stomped to the ground early on in the game so you're ultimately chasing a ghost.

Edit: So I've actually forced myself to finish the game and it got even worse so here we go more paragraphs. Also spoiler warning for those who want to for some reason play this.

Starting off with the quests, the tasks and sidequest that i've worked my ass off completing were an absolute waste of time. I've read about how the leveling system works and what the max cap is. So, the leveling system is basically scaled which means that the more stronger you get, the stronger the enemies get. This in literally any other game would have been okay but of course the devs found a way to ♥♥♥♥ this up because what this means is that all you have to do is play through just the story quests which is about 10 hours worth of content and you're all set! So now I'm stuck here with my embarassing 50 hours all for nothing. This isn't all however!! The max level cap is 132 (no idea why probably multiplayer), the thing is you stop getting stronger after level 80. You could argue that no sane person would ever try to reach level 80 but that doesn't erase the fact that the game [b] punishes [/b] you for actually playing the game and leveling up. There is literally [b] zero [/b] reason to play most of the game because the enemies will never be stronger than you until lvl 81.

Now here is the spoiler part. If you've played the game you probably remember that the game keeps telling you how important the choices you make are and how it shapes the world around Ryder, well all of that seems to have run out of budget. There is one ending, [b] one [/b]. It doesn't matter what you say or what you do to anyone, you'll still get only one happily ever after ending and that's it. The only thing that your choices change are the deaths of characters that have about 12 minutes of combined screentime that aren't even important to the story. That's it. The whole gimmick and charm that the original trilogy had with it's world building and decision making? Completely out the window, there's none of that. I should also note that no matter what you cannot make a single bad choice and if there is something mildly lukewarm the characters just glide over it like it never happened (I wonder what game reminds me of this?). So yeah, you're ultimately playing a linear rpg with a dialogue feature, that's it.

Last thing I want to share and what I found probably the most dissapointing is that the story of the game has been left unfinished. We never got to know who the original creators of the remnant were (all we know is what they were called), which is by the way one of the biggest mysteries the game has set, throughout the whole game you were met with the remnant, and yet it's all been left in the dust. This could have been such a good Dwemer from Skyrim moment (what happened to them? Why are they missing? Do they still exist?) this however has never been questioned in the game and never explained and taken further, it was simply abandoned. Another lose twist is the scourge: this one is even more of a mystery and once again has never been explained like what it truly is and what it's purpose is. The game has set these interesting plot points that they could have built off of and yet they decided that the most important thing in the game is to make sure that the Archon dies and everyone lives their lives on a beautiful planet and everyone dies old of natural causes. Great.
6/7 great game not the same as the OG but very close.
underrated due to its superior predecessor-trilogy. Game is still good tho.

when i first played this game i didnt get why people where being so harsh on it, then i played the OGs and now i realise that those games just set a very high standard, i still think mass effect andromeda can be an enjoyable experience, its just a different concept, i personally liked the aspect of finding a new world to settle on pretty interesting and i liked the characters (disclaimer im not finsished with the story yet)
